doc.body:
# Explicit interactive terminal ownership

spawn binds stdin and stdout to the supplied open terminal handle. It never
inherits the calling program's terminal implicitly. The caller owns that handle
and its terminal output; Attachment owns the child and bounded binary stderr.
close stops and reaps only that child, leaves the handle open, and does not stop
the daemon or other clients. Cancellation applies to startup, not the later
interactive lifetime. Use close to end that lifetime.

spawn proves OS process creation only. state starts as AttachmentPending;
inspect-client makes one explicit listing and records AttachmentAttached when
the owned PID is present. Child exit independently records AttachmentExited.
There is no polling loop or implicit readiness claim. An event from a separately
owned control connection may supply application-specific readiness evidence.

The initial session read checks Linux daemon identity, and the attach command
runs in a PID/start-time fence. The Engine's documented same-PID/same-second
replacement and normal builtin-dispatch assumptions also apply here. An exit
Result describes the tmux client process, not the lifetime of its session.
Refuse copying an owner, which would duplicate cleanup authority over one child.

doc.body:
# Partial outcomes, not transactions

Operation requires either acknowledgement-only or a Promise of Evidence. In
command scope, Complete means a successful command acknowledgement; it does not
prove an asynchronous external effect. In effect scope, Complete additionally
requires matching named Evidence with satisfied=True. Evidence is supplied by
the caller, who must arm and correlate its operation-specific observer before
dispatch. A name match is not proof of causation. No caller callback runs inside
the batch. Its deadline bounds waiting, not the caller's independent work.
Evidence Promises are one-shot: rerunning effect-aware commands requires newly
armed evidence, rather than treating an old observation as a new completion.

The immutable Batch captures finite membership, preserving order and rejecting
duplicate names. Empty membership is a no-op. run/run-async accept an existing
Runtime, Control connection or compatible CommandExecutor and never close it.
Adapters must validate without effects, honor absolute deadlines and cancellation,
settle their execution Promises with Receipt values, and preserve effect certainty
in typed errors.
All operations share one absolute deadline. A supplied ` :deadline(Instant) `
can shorten the local ` timeout-ms ` budget; it never extends that budget. The
same Instant is passed to every command and retained in the report. An already
expired deadline skips dispatch. The executor may use a shorter local limit. Cleanup retains
the executor's own separate bounds. Cancelling a dispatched Control request can
close that connection according to its documented delivery contract.

Every position receives an OperationResult. Failure stops subsequent dispatch
by default; on-error=continue attempts remaining operations while time and
cancellation permit. Never-dispatched suffixes are Skipped. A timed out or lost
in-flight effect is Indeterminate, even if acknowledgement was received. The
original exception and its outcome remain available through error/error-outcome.
No rollback is attempted or promised, and reports retain no executor owner.

output-budget-bytes defaults to 8 MiB. After each operation, Batch counts receipt
output and Command exception stdout/stderr, following shared Command causes only
once. Reaching or exceeding the threshold stops further dispatch even under
on-error=continue. The complete threshold-crossing receipt/error is retained and
the undispatched suffix is Skipped. This is an admission threshold: retained
output can reach the budget plus one executor-bounded response. It is not a hard
RSS cap; object overhead, arbitrary adapter/evidence exceptions and independent
caller-owned tasks remain outside that bound. Such adapters must accurately
report Receipt.output-bytes and bound their own responses.
A finite replayable sequence of explicit commands, without transaction semantics.
doc.summary: A finite replayable sequence of explicit commands, without transaction semantics.

doc.body:
# Capability observations
Construction consumes explicit observations and packaged catalogue data. It
never launches tmux. Replacing a daemon or negotiating connection flags needs
a new capability object. The engine binds these observations to actual
daemon identity; this class does not establish that identity by itself.

` supports ` and ` require ` describe native features. A fallback identifies an
alternative which the caller must choose explicitly. ` workaround ` describes
required handling; it never claims the repair was performed. Field support
does not mean the field was acquired or is available in every context.

## Features and required handling



- ` managed-commands `

feature; refuse; since 3.3a. Managed commands require an exact declared daemon release profile.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/cmd.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/cmd.c)



- ` format-tilde `

feature; refuse; since 3.3a. Six ordered substitutions encode delimiters, backslashes and dollar signs.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/format.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/format.c)



- ` format-argument-quote `

feature; fallback; since 3.7. q/a is introduced in 3.7; older profiles use the tested tilde codec.

Fallback: ` format-tilde `.



Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/81f88f8517c9fc5371b56cf117530c6b477c96ac/format.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/81f88f8517c9fc5371b56cf117530c6b477c96ac/format.c)



- ` format-output-vis `

defect; repair; exact releases 3.4, 3.5, 3.5a. Reverse one VIS output layer before decoding the tilde field.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/9ae69c3795ab5ef6b4d760f6398cd9281151f632/server-client.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/9ae69c3795ab5ef6b4d760f6398cd9281151f632/server-client.c)



- ` layout-classic `

feature; refuse; since 3.3a. Classic layouts remain available for old layouts and unnegotiated control clients.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/layout-custom.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/layout-custom.c)



- ` layout-json `

feature; refuse; since 3.8. JSON layouts include floating placements in the current profile.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53/layout-custom.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53/layout-custom.c)



- ` control-mode `

feature; refuse; since 3.3a. Control framing is available at the support floor.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/control.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/control.c)



- ` control-new-layouts `

feature; refuse; since 3.8. Enable new-layouts explicitly before interpreting new control layouts.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53/server-client.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53/server-client.c)



- ` pane-floating `

feature; refuse; since 3.7. Floating panes and their coordinates are available starting in 3.7.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/81f88f8517c9fc5371b56cf117530c6b477c96ac/cmd-split-window.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/81f88f8517c9fc5371b56cf117530c6b477c96ac/cmd-split-window.c)



- ` pane-modal `

feature; refuse; since 3.8. Modal panes and modal-window fields require 3.8.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53/cmd-split-window.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53/cmd-split-window.c)



- ` buffer-full `

feature; fallback; since 3.6. Use save-buffer when buffer_full is unavailable.

Fallback: ` buffer-save `.



Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0dac7fe434d029a4f0b819cba8eb7963df291990/format.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0dac7fe434d029a4f0b819cba8eb7963df291990/format.c)



- ` buffer-save `

feature; refuse; since 3.3a. Binary save-buffer capture is separate from FORMAT framing.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/cmd-save-buffer.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/cmd-save-buffer.c)



- ` layout-mirrored-main `

feature; refuse; since 3.5. Mirrored main-horizontal and main-vertical layouts require 3.5.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/ac44566c9c7e3e94d23be6def4c7ae83472543f5/layout-set.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/ac44566c9c7e3e94d23be6def4c7ae83472543f5/layout-set.c)



- ` split-percent-defect `

defect; refuse; exact releases 3.4. split-window -p is broken in 3.4; use the explicit -l percentage form.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/9ae69c3795ab5ef6b4d760f6398cd9281151f632/cmd-split-window.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/9ae69c3795ab5ef6b4d760f6398cd9281151f632/cmd-split-window.c)



- ` break-pane-name-defect `

defect; refuse; exact releases 3.7. tmux 3.7 ignores explicit break-pane names and dereferences a null name in the unnamed multi-pane path; refuse break-pane before dispatch.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/81f88f8517c9fc5371b56cf117530c6b477c96ac/cmd-break-pane.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/81f88f8517c9fc5371b56cf117530c6b477c96ac/cmd-break-pane.c)



- ` name-separator-defect `

defect; refuse; exact releases 3.7. tmux 3.7 rejects colon and dot names; validate their capability before dispatch.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/81f88f8517c9fc5371b56cf117530c6b477c96ac/tmux.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/81f88f8517c9fc5371b56cf117530c6b477c96ac/tmux.c)



- ` session-name-separators `

feature; refuse; since 3.7a. Literal dot and colon in session names require 3.7a; earlier releases replace or reject them.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0e418b62d259ce8da8970f75732cc6632ee4c3a0/tmux.c#L285](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0e418b62d259ce8da8970f75732cc6632ee4c3a0/tmux.c#L285)



- ` window-name-separators `

feature; refuse; since 3.3a. Literal dot and colon in window names are supported unless the declared separator defect applies.



Blocked by: name-separator-defect.

Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/window.c#L405](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0b355ae8114511e1ff6359272b164f1cdf718e80/window.c#L405)



- ` pane-empty-flag `

feature; refuse; since 3.7. Explicit empty split panes use -E from 3.7; older releases require the declared empty-argument adapter.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/81f88f8517c9fc5371b56cf117530c6b477c96ac/cmd-split-window.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/81f88f8517c9fc5371b56cf117530c6b477c96ac/cmd-split-window.c)



- ` window-empty `

feature; refuse; since 3.8. Empty window creation requires the new-window -E flag from 3.8.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53/cmd-new-window.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53/cmd-new-window.c)



- ` break-pane-single-print `

feature; refuse; since 3.6. Breaking the only pane prints its returned identity from 3.6; older releases need an explicit scoped identity acquisition.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0dac7fe434d029a4f0b819cba8eb7963df291990/cmd-break-pane.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0dac7fe434d029a4f0b819cba8eb7963df291990/cmd-break-pane.c)



- ` pane-floating-move `

feature; refuse; since 3.8. Floating pane position and stack changes require move-pane placement flags from 3.8.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53/cmd-join-pane.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53/cmd-join-pane.c)



- ` control-job-output `

feature; refuse; since 3.5. Foreground run-shell job output is delivered to the command client from 3.5; earlier releases send it to pane view mode. This does not guarantee shell-output framing.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/ac44566c9c7e3e94d23be6def4c7ae83472543f5/cmd-run-shell.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/ac44566c9c7e3e94d23be6def4c7ae83472543f5/cmd-run-shell.c)



- ` menu-appearance `

feature; refuse; since 3.4. Menu border, style, selected style and initial choice flags are available from 3.4.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/9ae69c3795ab5ef6b4d760f6398cd9281151f632/cmd-display-menu.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/9ae69c3795ab5ef6b4d760f6398cd9281151f632/cmd-display-menu.c)



- ` menu-mouse `

feature; refuse; since 3.5. The display-menu -M flag enables mouse selection without a triggering mouse event from 3.5.

- ` popup-close-on-key `

feature; refuse; since 3.6. The display-popup -k flag requests close on any key from 3.6.

feature; refuse; since 3.6. The display-popup -N flag resets existing popup flags from 3.6; omitted flags otherwise preserve the existing popup policy.





Source: [https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0dac7fe434d029a4f0b819cba8eb7963df291990/cmd-display-menu.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/0dac7fe434d029a4f0b819cba8eb7963df291990/cmd-display-menu.c)

- ` activity-action `

doc.body:
# Client commands

ClientTarget retains endpoint and daemon identity values only. Each operation
lists clients and checks the observed name, process ID and creation time before
dispatch. tmux exposes no permanent client ID: disconnect and name reuse between
this check and the command remain possible. The daemon fence does not make that
check atomic. A client target never silently selects a current client.
The read-only toggle follows tmux's paired read-only/ignore-size flag behavior;
it retains the observed session and suppresses environment updates.

Pane-context UI methods require an explicit pane belonging to the client's
current session. This avoids display-message's missing-target fallback. Pane
modes are shared by every client viewing that pane, not private UI state.

Menu, prompt, popup and pane-number methods return Promises and require an
explicit timeout in milliseconds. Human interaction may outlast that budget.
Cancellation or timeout stops the command client; it does not retract an overlay
or command already submitted. Use close-popup explicitly when appropriate.
Results describe command completion, not rendered pixels or a human response.

Literal messages disable FORMAT and strftime interpolation. tmux display styles
still apply. Menu labels retain display styles and leading-minus disabled-entry
semantics. CommandTemplate deliberately exposes tmux template syntax and percent
substitutions; it is never compiled as Raku. Popup shell-command deliberately
requests shell execution. Other commands use argv and the shared tmux encoder.
A value-only client target. No subprocess or connection is retained.
doc.summary: A value-only client target. No subprocess or connection is retained.

doc.body:
# Interpretation boundaries

Invocation encodes a tmux command, not a shell command or a FORMAT literal.
Double quoting alone does not suppress tmux tilde expansion. Exact octal
escapes preserve quotes, backslashes, dollars, tildes, controls and high bytes.
The encoded size limit applies after expansion and before dispatch.

Engine code inserts command separators deliberately between Invocation values;
literal semicolons inside their argument values remain data. Commands which
interpret FORMAT syntax require an additional command-specific policy.



# Single-operation admission

Effectful entry points use ` is single-operation ` to reject Junction arguments
before Raku can autothread a typed method into several operations. Unknown named
arguments are rejected unless the method explicitly forwards a slurpy options
hash; the receiving operation validates those forwarded names. Nested command
operands remain the responsibility of Invocation and the command's validators.
Native signatures, defaults and constraints retain their normal binding rules.
An effectful multi must guard its explicit proto, since candidate dispatch can
autothread before a wrapper on an individual candidate runs.
Role methods use capture admission in the proto body before typed candidate
dispatch. Wrapping an unspecialized role method loses its private-method context
after precompilation on the pinned compiler.

` is single-operation('async') ` returns one broken Promise for rejected input or
a synchronous exception from the method. Junctions and unknown names produce
` X::LibTmux::Command ` with ` kind ` argument and ` outcome ` NotStarted. Native
binding errors and exceptions from the body retain their types. An accepted
method's Promise passes through unchanged. Portable query validation keeps its
own ` InvalidFilter ` policy, while local selections retain native Junction
matching.

Options, Environment, Buffers, Hooks and KeyBindings are value-only facades

doc.body:
# Control framing and delivery

Decoder frames bytes on LF and correlates all three numeric guard fields.
Notification-shaped lines within a response remain payload. PaneOutput keeps
octal-decoded bytes, including NUL and incomplete UTF-8; text decoding belongs
to a separate incremental consumer. UnknownEvent preserves future notifications.

The tmux wire protocol does not escape arbitrary command payloads from matching
their own terminal guard. Managed reads must use declared, prefixed projections;
raw command output cannot promise lossless framing for guard-shaped payloads.
A Response acknowledges dispatch. Its end guard does not establish completion
of a launched job, popup, detach, or other asynchronous effect.
Some queued jobs print outside response blocks. UnframedOutput preserves such
lines, but the protocol cannot distinguish arbitrary job text from notifications.

Event delivery is live, without replay. A late tap misses earlier events.
Each subscriber has an independently bounded queue and serial worker. A slow
subscriber overflows explicitly; a throwing callback terminates only its own
subscription. Closing a tap discards queued values. Owner completion drains
already accepted values before done; failure drains before quit. User callbacks
already executing cannot be cancelled, and owner teardown does not wait for them.

# Owned control connection

Connection connects to an exact session on an observed daemon. Startup verifies
the daemon again over the persistent connection. The ignore-size client flag
avoids changing pane dimensions. New layouts are negotiated when supported;
older profiles retain their native control layout representation.

Commands are serialized through one bounded queue. A separate unpredictable
FORMAT barrier correlates every response, including nested commands and jobs
which print after their end guard. A barrier means the tmux command queue reached
that point; background jobs and external effects still need domain-specific
completion evidence. Raw command output has the framing limitations described
by :obj:`LibTmux::Control <LibTmux::Control>`. Declared projections avoid arbitrary output delimiters.

Each request owns a deadline from admission. Cancelling an unsent request leaves
the connection usable. Timeout or cancellation after dispatch closes the whole
connection because later response ownership is uncertain. Effects already sent
remain indeterminate. Closing stops the client, not the daemon or launched jobs.

An event Supply is shared, live and bounded per subscriber. Reconnect requires a
new Connection and explicit snapshot acquisition; old requests and observations
never migrate automatically. Every connection has a distinct epoch.

# Daemon identity and explicit effects

Endpoint captures argv scope and sanitized environment without I/O. Runtime
owns its executor; Observation and Incarnation retain values only. Observing
capabilities reads the daemon's version separately from the client executable.
Prepared projections and references are bound to that daemon incarnation.

Managed commands check Linux boot ID and process start ticks, then enter one
tmux command-list branch fenced by PID and tmux start time. A replacement
between those steps is refused unless it reuses the same PID and the same
second-resolution start time. That narrow race remains outside this guarantee.
Persistent control connections provide a separate, connection-bound lifetime.

Identity probes use a nonce-bearing invalid command with an equals sign and
hyphen. They cannot match tmux command-alias keys or trigger display-message
hooks. Normal dispatch of canonical built-in commands is assumed; this is not
a protocol for authenticating a hostile daemon or rewriting its configuration.

Closing Runtime stops its owned clients. It does not stop the tmux daemon or
undo effects already performed. ` raw ` preserves execution bounds but provides
no managed identity or compatibility guarantee. Text passed to a command may
still have command-specific FORMAT semantics beyond command-language quoting.

# Declared FORMAT projections
A Projection validates ordered catalogue field names, acquisition context,
capabilities, and nullable-field dependencies before generating a template.
Its schema identifies the field order, codec, and output-repair profile.
The separately retained incarnation binds a prepared projection to a daemon;
the engine validates that identity before dispatch.

Feed binary output to FrameDecoder and call finish at process completion.
An incomplete record, malformed token, exceeded bound, or mismatched schema
throws X::LibTmux::Decode and closes the decoder. Row numbers start at one;
offsets count bytes from the start of the response. Field conversion errors
identify the field's starting offset; token errors locate the offending byte.

DecodedRow.bytes retains exact immutable payload bytes. Its value method

# Observed layouts
Construct layouts and their cells through ` decode-layout `; direct ` new `
calls are refused so captured bytes and validated structure stay together.

Classic layouts validate their checksum and represented tiled tree; ` 0000, `

all cells, including floating placements with signed coordinates and z-index.

empty string means known absence, while omission means not acquired.

traversal perform no I/O. Input bytes, nesting, numeric spelling and node
counts are bounded before or during parsing.

doc.body:
# Captured graph

Snapshot captures observations over an interval. Its field accessors, raw bytes,
relations and typed selections perform no I/O. It retains endpoint settings and
incarnation values, never the Runtime that acquired it. Reference construction
is local; reference commands create and close a fresh bounded client executor.

Physical windows and panes are unique by scoped ID. WindowLink represents one
session/index association, including repeated links to the same physical window.
Raw contextual rows preserve their multiplicity. Contradictory duplicate records
and missing targets in complete collections raise InconsistentSnapshot.
An incomplete relation raises MissingData rather than appearing empty.

same-entity compares daemon-scoped identity. WindowLink has no stable identity
between captures, so its comparison is confined to one captured graph. A link
reference checks its expected physical window before selecting or unlinking;
renumbering between that check and the operation remains a documented race.

Window.decoded-layout parses captured layout bytes locally. Strict text access
can fail for invalid UTF-8 while bytes remains available.



# Explicit commands

SessionRef.new-window and PaneRef.split/new-floating return references from the
command's declared identity projection. PaneRef.break returns the resulting
WindowRef; older profiles that omit the identity for a single-pane break use
an ID-filtered observation afterward. A new observation is acquired only by
inspect. If the source window has several placements, break requires an
explicit :from(WindowLinkRef) so tmux cannot choose which association to move.
Other mutations return a command Result. Completion means the tmux
client completed; pane input processing, rendering and child programs may
continue afterward.

WindowRef.link and WindowLinkRef.move require a destination session and index.
They return a WindowLinkRef for that placement. Moving, swapping or unlinking a
placement is separate from WindowRef.kill, which destroys the physical window
and all its links. tmux synchronizes placement changes across grouped sessions;
unlinking a placement also removes its corresponding peer placements. Physical
window linking prefers the destination session's existing source context when
the window is already present there. Link checks and mutations are separate operations;
concurrent renumbering can race between them. Cross-daemon targets are rejected.

References expose value-only options and hooks facades; SessionRef also exposes
environment. Creating these facades performs no I/O. Their get, set and other
methods explicitly acquire or mutate current configuration. See
:obj:`LibTmux::Configuration <LibTmux::Configuration>` for typed option, environment and command-value rules.

Client.ref creates a ClientRef with the observed name bytes, PID and creation
time. inspect requires that identity to remain attached. Client commands are
inherited from :obj:`LibTmux::Client <LibTmux::Client>`; client disconnection and name reuse can still
race between the identity check and the command.

Names and start directories are literal. Names that tmux would silently change
are refused, and separator support follows the daemon's capability profile.
PaneRef.set-title quotes one FORMAT expansion; tmux's title validation still
applies. The low-level command method keeps native tmux argument semantics.
Shell commands passed to creation and respawn run through tmux's shell-command
contract. PaneRef.pipe deliberately accepts tmux FORMAT and strftime syntax as
well as shell syntax. It closes an existing pipe when called without a command;
:toggle follows pipe-pane -o, which closes an already open pipe.

Literal pane input uses send-text and never appends Enter. send-keys accepts
key names and a positive :repeat. capture and capture-pending return Blob data
without text conversion or whitespace removal. copy-command sends an explicit
copy-mode command; it does not interpret arbitrary text as a key sequence.
reset queues terminal-state reset followed by history clearing without a client
roundtrip between them. It is not transactional: failure can leave partial
effects. reset-terminal only resets terminal state. Running a shell's ` reset `
program is a separate application action: send-text('reset') followed by
send-keys('Enter') requests it without promising what the pane application does.

Split dimensions use :size or :percent exclusively. Percentage splits use the
size syntax across profiles, avoiding the known percentage-flag defect. Empty
pane creation selects its documented profile encoding; empty windows require
the corresponding capability. Floating creation, movement, stacking, modal
panes and layout variants have independent capability checks. The defective
break-pane profile is refused before either named or unnamed operations.

See :obj:`LibTmux::Server <LibTmux::Server>` for endpoint ownership and acquisition,
:obj:`LibTmux::Selection <LibTmux::Selection>` for captured collection operations, and
:obj:`LibTmux::Transport <LibTmux::Transport>` for Result and process cancellation contracts.

doc.body:
# Validated local criteria

` Filter.compile(%criteria, :entity<pane>) ` validates and copies one
criterion before any entity is read. ` matches($view) ` and native smartmatching
through ` ACCEPTS ` use the same evaluator. The view protocol has four fixed
methods: ` entity `, ` state($name) `, ` value($name) ` and ` relation($name) `.
Names are checked against the catalogue; input keys never become method calls.

Field values abbreviate equality. Operator mappings support ` equals `,
` not-equals `, ` in `, ` not-in `, numeric ` lt/lte/gt/gte `, literal ` contains `,
` starts-with `, ` ends-with `, and nullable fields' ` is-null `. Operators and
fields at the same level are conjoined. Numeric operands exclude Bool and
non-finite values. Text is NFC normalized and literal matching compares
codepoints, including positions inside a grapheme. Invalid UTF8-C8 bytes are
refused; byte comparison belongs to a separate interface.

` AND ` and ` OR ` accept collections of complete criteria. ` NOT ` accepts one
criterion. Empty criteria and AND are true; empty OR and in are false; empty
not-in is true. Boolean evaluation short-circuits after schema validation.
For example, an OR whose first branch matches does not read an unloaded field
in its second branch. Unknown fields in either branch still fail compilation.

To-many relations support ` some `, ` every ` and ` none `. One ` some ` requires
one child to satisfy its complete subtree. Separate existential subtrees may
use different children. Loaded empty relations yield false, true and true,
respectively. To-one relations support ` is `, ` is-not `, and ` is-null ` where
the relation is nullable. No evaluation performs I/O.

KnownNull satisfies only an explicit null test. For example,
` dead-status => %(not-equals => 0) ` is false when status is KnownNull;
` NOT => %(dead-status => %(not-equals => 0)) ` is true. Likewise a
null group fails both ` is ` and ` is-not `. Unsupported, Unavailable and Unloaded
states throw MissingData when evaluated. They are never empty relations,
empty strings, zero or false.

` criteria ` exposes normalized nested Maps and Lists. ` ast ` exposes immutable
nodes for source planning: kind, entity, name, wire-name, operator, field-kind,
target, operand and children. Cloning a Filter is refused; compile changed data
to preserve validation. Native callbacks, Junctions, regexes, type objects,
lazy collections and cycles are not criterion data.



# Proposed JSON representation

` to-json ` and ` Filter.from-json(Str|Blob) ` use JSON::Fast and the proposed
` libtmux.where/v1 ` envelope with exactly ` schema `, ` entity ` and ` where `.
This is a Raku proposal, not a claim of tested cross-port wire compatibility.
Catalogue wire names are stable camelCase names; compound operator names use
camelCase too, such as ` notEquals `, ` startsWith `, ` isNull ` and ` isNot `.
JSON::Fast uses the last value for a duplicate object key.
The bounded preflight also rejects malformed numeric spellings and raw control
characters in strings; parsing remains delegated to JSON::Fast.

Wire numbers use finite binary64 values bounded in absolute magnitude by
` 2**53-1 `, with integers in that safe range kept exact. Decimal JSON operands
are interpreted as binary64. Export of an exact Rat or FatRat requires a
power-of-two denominator, a numerator below 2**53 in absolute magnitude and
a lossless nonzero binary64 conversion. In particular, local ` 1/3 ` criteria
remain valid but cannot be serialized by rounding to ` 0.333333 `. JSON numeric
tokens are limited to 64 characters and exponents to absolute value 324;
overflow and nonzero underflow are refused.

Limits defaults are 1 MiB wire input/output, depth 32, 4096 copied value nodes
and 1024 membership operands. Byte length and structural JSON depth are checked
before parsing while respecting quoted strings and escapes. Native and decoded
criteria then share bounded recursive validation. Supply an immutable Limits
value to compile or from-json to choose tighter limits.

# Planning an explicit read

` Plan.compile($filter, :$capabilities) ` performs no I/O. ` auto ` uses proven
scalar restrictions; ` never ` leaves filtering local; ` require ` throws unless
the complete predicate has an exact source implementation. The capability
value must come from the daemon incarnation that will execute the read.

For ` acquisition-mode ` ` listing `, pass ` projection ` and ` candidate-command `
together to the guarded reader. The command does not include ` -F `: the reader
adds the projection's template. Normalize physical entity IDs or session/index
link keys according to ` identity-normalization `, then apply ` matches ` to every
candidate. It always evaluates the original validated filter, including when
` fully-pushed ` is true.

For ` full-graph `, acquire one complete snapshot and apply ` matches ` to its
root entities. Do not execute the candidate command. ` source-filter ` is empty;
` acquisition-reason ` explains why an otherwise eligible scalar restriction is
deferred. ` required-relations ` retains each relationship path. Filtering child
rows first would change ` every ` and ` none `, and intersecting a separately
acquired candidate set with a later graph can lose matches during mutation.



# Inspecting source work

` steps ` exposes the translation tree, paths, exactness, expressions and refusal
reasons. Eligible conjuncts can restrict candidates while text remains local.
An AND restriction follows the captured evaluator order and stops at the first
residual subtree, retaining that subtree's own safe prefix if present. It never
moves a later restriction ahead of local work that may throw. Use an explicit
AND array when the ordering of residual evaluation matters; hash iteration is
not an ordering contract.
An OR or NOT subtree is emitted only when the complete subtree is exact.
Text and relationship predicates remain local. Empty Boolean and membership
nodes retain the same identities as the local query evaluator.

ID matching uses tmux string equality. Flags use exact zero/one equality.
Numeric comparisons use arithmetic FORMAT expressions, never lexical ordering.
The catalogue records source-proven UInt32 dimension and nonnegative Int32
window-index domains. Only integer operands within the exact IEEE-754 integer
range are eligible. Bounded operands alone cannot establish source equivalence:
the observed field's complete domain must also fit the arithmetic conversion.
Fractional operands, nullable fields and unqualified numeric fields stay local.

Boolean expressions are balanced and bounded by bytes and nesting depth. An
oversized expression remains local under ` auto ` and is refused by ` require `.
The guarded reader still enforces its own complete command/output/time limits.

# Captured selections

A concrete selection consumes ` Selection[Pane, 'pane'] ` or another catalogue
entity schema. ` new(:items) ` copies finite, eager, defined membership. It does
not deep-clone member objects. Observation classes must supply their own
read-only field contract.

Binding ` my @panes := $snapshot.panes ` preserves the selection. Array
assignment materializes ordinary array membership; assigning to a scalar
itemizes the selection. Use ` $panes.List ` when explicit list traversal is
wanted. Each iterator and Seq is fresh. Array conversion is independently
mutable; List membership cannot be replaced.

` where ` accepts criterion data or a compiled Filter and validates the schema
before traversal. ` filter ` invokes one callback per member, eagerly in source
order, and throws a directly returned Failure before Boolean coercion. Both
return the same concrete selection type and preserve order and duplicates.
Native ` grep `, ` map `, ` sort `, ` first ` and junctions delegate to the captured
List, including grep adverbs. They retain native return and evaluation rules.
` one ` constructs a junction; exact cardinality uses ` single `.

# Server ownership

` new ` captures a borrowed endpoint without I/O. ` snapshot ` and ` capabilities `
acquire daemon state explicitly. ` new-session ` requires an existing daemon,
creates a detached session, and returns a SessionRef from tmux's returned ID.
Names are literal Unicode text; controls, backslash, dot and colon are refused
before creation because supported tmux releases normalize them differently.
A shell-command explicitly requests tmux's shell-command interpretation.

` start ` creates a clean foreground daemon on an exclusive temporary socket,
verifies its executable profile before launch, binds its actual process identity,
and creates the initial session. The startup timeout covers all stages. Linux
inotify socket attributes signal listener readiness; pidfds bind termination to
the original process, independently of socket reuse.

Close is idempotent and joins owned work. Borrowed daemons remain running.
Owned daemons receive TERM followed by bounded KILL escalation and are reaped.
Cleanup removes only the original socket and empty original directory; unknown
files and replacement sockets are preserved. References retain values only and
are not clients owned by the Server. A stopped owned daemon invalidates them.

Configuration factories perform one explicit identity observation. The returned
facades retain endpoint and incarnation values, and each subsequent configuration
operation owns its temporary command client. ` open-control ` and ` attach ` return
separate lifecycle owners: callers must close them. Closing a borrowed Server
does not close those owners; closing an owned daemon causes its attached clients
to disconnect. ` attach ` proves process creation, not terminal readiness.

` command ` is an explicit tmux-syntax escape hatch with a daemon fence. It does
not insert an entity target or interpret shell syntax on the caller's behalf.
` run-batch ` reports partial outcomes and never promises rollback.



# Explicit environment and health

` from-env ` is the only factory that interprets ` TMUX `. It parses its final
PID and session components from the right, so commas in the socket path remain
literal. It requires an absolute socket path, validates ` TMUX_PANE ` when
present, observes the actual daemon and rejects a different PID. The returned
borrowed facade is bound to that incarnation. Child processes still receive
neither ambient variable. Imported object IDs are observations from the supplied
environment, not evidence that those objects still exist:

use LibTmux;
my $server = LibTmux::Server.from-env(:environment(%*ENV));
LEAVE $server.close;
my $snapshot = $server.snapshot;
my $pane = $snapshot.panes.where(%(id => $server.environment-pane-id)).single;
my $window = $pane.window;
my $session = $snapshot.sessions
    .where(%(id => $server.environment-session-id)).single;

The selection throws for a vanished object or absent imported ID. A window can
belong to several sessions; the imported session ID supplies that context.
` capabilities ` is the explicit native health observation: success returns
verified daemon evidence, while connection, identity and permission failures
retain their original typed exceptions. ` has-session(:name) ` and
` has-session(:id) ` return false only after a successful exact listing finds
no match. ` kill-server ` deliberately terminates the observed daemon, including
a borrowed one; ` close ` continues to preserve borrowed daemons. An owner must
still close after kill-server to join its process and filesystem cleanup.



# Jobs and channels

` run-shell ` receives literal shell source; tmux FORMAT-looking text is escaped
before dispatch. ` if-shell ` follows the same rule for its shell condition and
accepts bounded Invocation values for both branches. Its explicit ` :format `
option instead evaluates a native tmux FORMAT condition. ` source-file ` reads
one literal pathname, escaping native glob metacharacters; it does not expand
FORMAT, tilde or a caller shell. Relative paths use the captured command cwd.
` :parse-only ` parses configuration without executing it.

Each request shares one admission, observation and dispatch deadline. A
background job acknowledges scheduling. Foreground completion follows tmux's
job/command queue contract, not an application-specific postcondition; command
output availability also depends on the declared daemon profile. Timing out or
cancelling a client does not undo a job, configuration effect or channel lock
already accepted by the daemon. ` wait-for ` offers only wait, signal, lock and
unlock; it does not claim that a signal proves another process's application
work completed.



# Administrative commands

Diagnostics and administrative commands intentionally use the explicit bounded
Invocation surface rather than separate wrappers. These complete calls retain
raw stdout/stderr in Result, enforce the server deadline and throw typed command
errors. ` list-commands `, ` show-messages `, ` lock-server ` and ` server-access `
are deliberate replacements for named Python helpers, not claims of identical
typed parameters. ` switch-mode ` is also available through Invocation.

use LibTmux;
my $server = LibTmux::Server.start(:name<inspection>);
LEAVE $server.close;
my $commands = $server.command(Invocation.new(:argv(['list-commands'])));
my $access = $server.command(Invocation.new(:argv(['server-access', '-l'])));
my $messages = $server.command(Invocation.new(:argv(['show-messages', '-T'])));
$server.command(Invocation.new(:argv(['lock-server'])));

Administrative flags keep tmux's native semantics and errors; arbitrary
Invocation values do not acquire a typed catalogue guarantee. Locking may run
configured lock commands on attached clients. Access changes affect other users.
Use only an endpoint whose administration the caller owns or has authorized.
To detach captured clients, iterate ` $snapshot.clients ` and call each
` .ref.detach `. Each target is identity guarded; a changing client set is not
an atomic detach-all operation, and acknowledgement does not prove terminal
rendering or child-process exit.

# Bounded child processes

Executor accepts a nonempty positional argv of defined, NUL-free strings.
It invokes that executable directly. Shell syntax, tmux command syntax and
FORMAT expansion belong to callers above this layer.

` execute ` returns a Result. ` execute-async ` always returns a Promise,
including for invalid arguments or closed admission. Each call copies argv,
environment entries and input bytes before asynchronous work begins. An
omitted environment copies the current environment; an explicit empty mapping
passes no variables. Input is a Blob, and the child receives EOF after those
bytes are written. Both output streams are binary and drain concurrently.

` timeout-ms ` bounds an admitted operation, ` max-output-bytes ` bounds combined
retained stdout/stderr, and ` cleanup-timeout-ms ` bounds waiting after forced
termination. Their defaults are 10000 ms, 8388608 bytes and 1000 ms. All are
positive integers. Encoded tmux command size has a separate Engine policy.
` execute ` and ` execute-async ` accept an optional ` timeout-ms ` override for
callers sharing one deadline across several child operations.

By default a nonzero exit or signal throws X::LibTmux::Command. ` :!check `
returns its Result with outcome Failed instead. Spawn failure, invalid input,
timeout, cancellation, output overflow and I/O failures still throw. Error
records retain bounded output bytes, process identity and reaping evidence.
NotStarted means no child effects were admitted. Failed and Indeterminate do
not mean that earlier effects were rolled back. Complete means child process
completion, not completion of a program controlled through tmux.

Cancellation is one shot. Dropping an operation Promise does not cancel its
child. Explicit cancellation and executor close terminate admitted children;
close callers share one Promise. A close failure remains observable on later
close calls. The executor owns direct child clients, not programs deliberately
started in a tmux pane or arbitrary descendant daemons.
Executor and Cancellation cannot be cloned. Result clones reconstruct and
validate replacement attributes, copying output bytes again.
One-shot cancellation shared by explicitly selected operations.
